## menu — Menu (component, archetype navigate)
A transient list of choices or commands revealed from a trigger.
Aliases: dropdown menu, context menu, overflow menu, menu bar, mega menu
Anatomy: Trigger (What opens the menu); Items (Choices and commands); Structure (Sections and submenus)
Related — neighbors: command-palette, popover
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Opening [invocation] — What opens it?
  - openBy (single-select: one id) — Opened by
      button-click: Button click (e.g. Overflow ⋮ menus)
      right-click-or-long-press: Right-click or long-press (e.g. Context menus)
      menu-bar: Menu bar (e.g. macOS menu bar)
      hover: Hover (e.g. Retail mega menus)
      keyboard: Keyboard (e.g. Alt to reach Windows menus)
* Structure [composition] — How are items organized?
  - structure (single-select: one id) — Structure
      flat: Flat (e.g. Overflow menus)
      sections: Sections (e.g. Google Docs menus)
      cascading-submenus: Cascading submenus (e.g. Desktop menu bars)
      mega-menu: Mega menu — Multi-column panel (e.g. Retail department menus)
* Item content [content] — What does each item show?
  - item (multi-select: list of ids) — Item content
      label: Label (e.g. All)
      icon: Icon (e.g. Google Docs)
      shortcut-hint: Shortcut hint (e.g. macOS menus)
      checkmark-state: Checkmark state (e.g. View menus)
      description: Description (e.g. GitHub menus)
* Item set [initiative] — Who decides which items appear and in what order?
  - itemSet (single-select: one id) — Item set
      fixed: Fixed (e.g. Most menus)
      depends-on-selection: Depends on selection (e.g. Context menus)
      adaptive: Adaptive — The system reorders by use (e.g. Office 2000 personalized menus)
      adaptable: Adaptable — The person reorders (e.g. Office Quick Access Toolbar)
* Form [layout] — What shape is it?
  - form (single-select: one id) — Form
      vertical-list: Vertical list (e.g. Most menus)
      radial: Radial (e.g. Blender pie menus)
      icon-grid: Icon grid (e.g. Google apps launcher)
      horizontal-bar: Horizontal bar (e.g. Toolbars)

## drawer — Drawer (component, archetype navigate)
A panel that slides in from a screen edge, holding navigation, detail, filters or an assistant beside the main content.
Aliases: side sheet, flyout panel, slide-over
Anatomy: Panel (The drawer surface); Scrim (What covers content when modal); Handle or trigger (What opens it)
Related — neighbors: modal-dialog, bottom-sheet, split-pane
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Edge and relationship [layout] — Which edge, and does it cover, push or sit beside content?
  - edge (single-select: one id) — Edge
      left: Left (e.g. Navigation drawers)
      right: Right (e.g. Detail panels)
      top: Top (e.g. Notification shades)
  - relationship (single-select: one id) — Relationship to content
      overlay-with-scrim: Overlay with scrim (e.g. Material modal navigation drawer)
      push-content: Push content (e.g. Standard drawers)
      docked: Docked (e.g. Material standard side sheet)
      overlay-no-scrim: Overlay, no scrim — The panel lies over the content without dimming or disabling it visually (GitHub Projects item panel, Notion side peek, OS panels) (e.g. GitHub Projects — Item side panel)
* Contents [content] — What is it for?
  - holds (single-select: one id) — Holds
      navigation: Navigation (e.g. Gmail on Android)
      item-detail: Item detail (e.g. GitHub Projects item panel)
      filters: Filters (e.g. Mobile retail)
      settings: Settings (e.g. Admin consoles)
      assistant: Assistant (e.g. Microsoft Edge Copilot sidebar)
      system-status-and-controls: System status and controls — Notifications, quick toggles and widgets belonging to the OS rather than the app (Android shade, iOS Control Center, Windows Widgets, macOS Notification Center) (e.g. Android — Notification shade)
      companion-apps: Companion apps — Small versions of ot

## agent-run — Agent run (pattern, archetype delegate-ai)
A goal-directed model session that plans and executes multiple steps with tools, while the person monitors, interrupts, approves and reviews the resulting changes.
Aliases: autonomous agent, tool-using agent, multi-step AI task
Anatomy: Goal (The assigned objective); Plan or trace (Steps the agent takes); Tools (Actions it may invoke); Artifacts (Files or states it changes); Approval gates (Human checkpoints)
Related — uses: prompt-input, ai-provenance, progress-indicator, confirmation, undo | specializes: delegate-ai | neighbors: ai-chat, status-tracker, node-editor
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Goal briefing [content] — What specifies the agent’s job?
  - brief (multi-select: list of ids) — Brief
      natural-language-goal: Natural-language goal (e.g. Cursor agent)
      checklist-of-acceptance-criteria: Checklist of acceptance criteria (e.g. Task agents)
      repo-or-workspace-context: Repo or workspace context (e.g. Coding agents)
      tool-allowlist: Tool allowlist (e.g. Computer-use permissions)
      budget-or-step-limit: Budget or step limit (e.g. Max turns)
* Step composition [composition] — How are steps, tools and artifacts structured?
  - structure (single-select: one id) — Structure
      linear-trace: Linear trace (e.g. Chat-style agent logs)
      plan-then-execute: Plan then execute (e.g. Planner–worker agents)
      dag-of-subagents: DAG of subagents (e.g. Parallel tool agents)
      single-tool-loop: Single tool loop (e.g. ReAct-style loops)
      human-in-the-loop-graph: Human-in-the-loop graph (e.g. Approval nodes)
* Run control [invocation] — How is a run started, steered and stopped?
  - control (multi-select: list of ids) — Control
      start-from-a-prompt: Start from a prompt (e.g. ChatGPT agent mode)
      continue-redirect-mid-run: Continue / redirect mid-run (e.g. Cursor)
      pause-for-approval: Pause for approval (e.g. Destructive tool confirms)
      stop-immediately: Stop immediately (e.g. Cancel run)
      schedule-or-retry: Schedule or retry (e.g. Background agents)
* Autonomy lifecycle [lifecycle] — How long does the agent act without a person?
  - lifecycle (single-select: one id) — Lifecycle
      seconds-few-tools: Seconds, few tools (e.g. Simple assistants)
      minutes-with-live-trace: Minutes with live trace (e.g. Cursor agent)
      long-running-background-job: Long-running background job (e.g. Overnight coding agents)
      persistent-memory-across-runs: Persistent memory across runs (e.g. Project agents)
      expires-without-heartbeat: Expires without heartbeat (e.g. Timed sessions)
* Progress feedback [feedback] — How does the person see what the agent is doing?
  - feedback (multi-select: list of ids) — Feedback
      streaming-step-log: Streaming step log (e.g. Cursor)
      file-diffs-as-they-land: File diffs as they land (e.g. Coding agents)
      screenshots-of-a-computer: Screenshots of a computer (e.g. Computer-use agents)
      todo-checklist-progress: Todo checklist progress (e.g. Plan UIs)
      errors-and-retries: Errors and retries (e.g. Tool failure traces)
      live-preview-of-the-artifact: Live preview of the artifact — The thing being built is rendered and running beside the trace — an app preview, a live document — so progress is judged from the artifact rather than from logs or diffs; the defining feedback of app-generation agents (e.g. Replit Agent — Build an app)
      cost-and-usage-meter: Cost and usage meter — Tokens, dollars or context used shown as the run proceeds, so the person can judge whether to let it continue; standard in agents where the person pays per call (e.g. Cline — VS Code extension agent)
* Approval initiative [initiative] — When must a person act during the run?
  - approvals (single-select: one id) — Approvals
      fully-autonomous-until-done: Fully autonomous until done (e.g. Low-risk digests)
      approve-each-tool-call: Approve each tool

## badge — Badge (component, archetype monitor)
A small indicator on another element showing a count or a status.
Aliases: counter, notification dot, status pill
Anatomy: Host (What it is attached to); Indicator (Count, dot or label)
Related — neighbors: stat-tile, progress-indicator
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Meaning [content] — What does the badge say?
  - meaning (single-select: one id) — Meaning
      count: Count (e.g. Unread messages)
      dot: Dot — Something new (e.g. App icon dots)
      status: Status (e.g. Online presence)
      label: Label (e.g. New or Beta)
* Overflow [encoding] — How are large counts shown?
  - overflow (single-select: one id) — Overflow
      exact-count: Exact count (e.g. Mail folders)
      capped: Capped — 99+ (e.g. Many apps)
      dot-past-a-threshold: Dot past a threshold (e.g. Minimal badges)
* What counts [initiative] — Who decides what increments it?
  - rule (single-select: one id) — Counting rule
      everything-unread: Everything unread (e.g. Default mail badges)
      only-mentions: Only mentions (e.g. Slack mentions-only badge setting)
      the-person-s-rule: The person’s rule (e.g. Custom inbox counts)
      pending-actions: Pending actions — The badge counts work waiting for the person — updates to install, apps to update, tasks to finish — rather than anything read, unread or addressed to them; the counting rules as written assume a message inbox (e.g. iOS Settings — App icon)
* Aggregation [scope] — Does it roll up?
  - aggregation (single-select: one id) — Aggregation
      per-item: Per item (e.g. Folder counts)
      rolled-up-to-parent: Rolled up to parent (e.g. Account totals)
      app-icon-total: App icon total (e.g. iOS app badges)
      device-total: Device total — One indicator for every unread notification on the device, on system chrome rather than on any app's icon or nav entry (watch faces, always-on displays) (e.g. Apple Watch — Watch face)

## ai-provenance — AI provenance (component, archetype delegate-ai)
Visible markers of what a model produced, from which sources or tools, so a person can judge trust, reuse and responsibility.
Aliases: generated label, AI disclosure, source attribution
Anatomy: Badge (That something is AI-involved); Source list (Citations or tools used); Detail (Expanded provenance); Action (Inspect, copy or report)
Related — uses: badge, tooltip, popover | neighbors: tooltip, badge, confirmation
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* What is disclosed [content] — What provenance facts are shown?
  - disclosure (multi-select: list of ids) — Disclosure
      ai-generated-badge: AI-generated badge (e.g. Doc AI labels)
      model-identity: Model identity (e.g. ChatGPT model name)
      citations: Citations (e.g. Perplexity sources)
      tool-calls-used: Tool calls used (e.g. Agent traces)
      human-vs-ai-edit-mix: Human vs AI edit mix (e.g. Suggestion mode authorship)
      training-data-unknown: Training-data unknown (e.g. Honest empty state)
      verification-highlighting: Verification highlighting — Sentence-level colour highlighting showing whether a live search corroborates or contradicts the claim, rather than a citation list or a static badge (e.g. Google Gemini — Double-check response)
* Provenance placement [layout] — Where do disclosure cues sit?
  - placement (single-select: one id) — Placement
      inline-beside-the-span: Inline beside the span (e.g. Ghost-text labels)
      header-of-a-reply: Header of a reply (e.g. Chat turns)
      footnote-citations: Footnote citations (e.g. Perplexity)
      hover-card: Hover card (e.g. Source previews)
      watermark-on-media: Watermark on media (e.g. Generated-image marks)
* Inspecting provenance [invocation] — How does a person open the full trail?
  - openBy (multi-select: list of ids) — Open by
      click-citation: Click citation (e.g. Perplexity)
      expand-tool-trace: Expand tool trace (e.g. ChatGPT)

Agent panels overflow the edges but have no scroll or advance controls; they look static
Feature detail opens as a right-side drawer, not a centred modal

aesthetics.typography: Inter Variable for everything: display headings, nav and body. Berkeley Mono for code, FIG labels, the caption under the logo strip and changelog dates.
aesthetics.typeScale: Big jump between display and UI text. H1 is 64px, section and CTA headings are 48px, the large blurbs are 20-24px, and nav, body and mockup UI use 12-15px. Headings are medium weight with tight tracking. There is little bold; muted grey tones carry the hierarchy.

label.notes: Near-black (#08090a) Linear marketing homepage. Almost all imagery is live-DOM product mockups, not bitmaps: the app shell, issue view and agent panel, a Slack thread, the kanban board, roadmap, scatter chart, agent panels and code diff. They fade out at the edges with gradient masks and sit on #0f1011 surfaces with 1px hairlines and 12px radii. The patterns coded from these mockups are depictions; the hero sidebar only highlights on click and does not navigate. The page's own interactive UI is the hover mega-menu, the Features + buttons that open a right drawer (TECH SPECS), pill buttons and text links with arrows. Sections are split by full-width hairlines, with a 2-column heading/blurb layout. The only saturated color is the lime Ramp testimonial and a pastel gradient OpenAI card; accents inside the mockups are status colors and the teal data dots. The customer logo strip and testimonials have no codebook entry; I filed a proposal (social-proof).
